newsitem.title: LATVIA: CUSTOMS, COMPANIES FORM CONSULTATIVE BODY.
newsitem.headline: CUSTOMS, COMPANIES FORM CONSULTATIVE BODY.

text.p: The finance ministry on Thursday said that in a long overdue move a consultative body of the customs management and businessmen has been formed, aimed at pointing out problems in the customs laws and system.
Complaints about inefficiencies have long plagued the customs system. A new law on customs is expected to be passed by the parliament at the end of May or beginning of June.

"The committee, which many say was long due, will point out the problems which prevent the improvement of the work of customs and transit flows," Aija Pocha, state revenues minister, told a news conference.
The committee will also serve as a forum for informing businessmen about expected changes, she added.
Businessmen were represented by the Association of Entrepreneurs, having direct contact with customs, such as the warehouse, traders and truck and transport associations.
The Latvian Chamber of Commerce of Industry and the British and U.S. Chambers of Commerce were also represented.
Manager of the Customs service Normunds Niedols was elected the head of the committee and its statutes are to be discussed on April 10.
The committee is expected to meet twice a month.
